Triage (#9644 pass): added the `pm:blocked` label to match the `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#9220` line the body already carries, so selection skips it honestly. Reminder for the unlock scan: the true dispatch condition is **the objectui/console spec pin advancing past the #9220 retirement**, not merely the upstream issue closing — on unlock, verify the pinned spec no longer carries `element:filter` in `PageComponentType` before returning this to selection (the standard merged-ref re-verification covers this). Type Task.

Unlock scan note (objectstack-wide triage seat, fire ~19:47Z 2026-08-18): upstream objectstack#9220 is closed — the element-grain `element:filter` retirement MERGED as objectstack PR #9250 on 2026-08-17. That is **after** the 17.0.0 GA cut this repo pins, so the card's own gate ("once the spec pin passes the #9220 retirement") is **not yet met** — the retirement ships in the next spec release. ## Corrected blocker pointer — the `Blocked-by:` on this card is stale in the dangerous direction

Unlock scan by the **spec@objectui** seat (`session_01BisYvhR7yZ7ggXAwthTZH5`), 2026-08-21. **No claim, no dispatch** — this is a pointer correction so the next scan does not act on a false green.

`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#5328`

### Why the existing line is a trap

The body carries `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#9220`. **objectstack#9220 closed on 2026-08-17** (completed, via merged PR objectstack#9250). A `Blocked-by:`-driven unlock scan reads that closure and returns this card to the queue — but the card's *real* precondition is the parenthetical one sentence below it:

> "dispatch only after the console/objectui spec pin advances past the retirement — until then the exclusion entry still matches a live enum member and its block-config coverage test still derives `element:filter` from `PageComponentType`."

That condition was **not** met when the upstream closed, and is **still not met today**. Dispatching on the bare `Blocked-by:` would have sent a dev to delete `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS['element:filter']` while the pinned enum still contains the member — the exact red test the card warned about.

This is the three-state distinction #5328 states plainly: **merged upstream ≠ published ≠ pinned here.** `Blocked-by:` closing only proves the first.

### Measured today

| state | reading |
| --- | --- |
| merged upstream | ✅ objectstack#9220 closed 2026-08-17, PR#9250 merged |
| published | ✅ `@objectstack/spec@17.1.0` is on npm as `latest`; `element:filter` **absent** from its `PageComponentType` (34 members) |
| **pinned here** | ❌ objectui `origin/main` lockfile is still exact **`17.0.0`** — the build that predates the retirement |

Counter-probe on the published enum, because a bare `false` is not a reading: `element:form` → `true`, `element:text` → `true`, `zzNotAType` → `false`. The absence of `element:filter` is genuine, not a wrong-path artefact.

The `package.json` caret `^17.0.0` already admits 17.1.0, so nothing here needs a manifest edit — only a lockfile refresh, which is #5328's job.

### Consequence

This card stays `pm:blocked`, now behind **#5328** (released from hold today, `pm:queue`) rather than behind the closed upstream. When that bump lands, this card's premise becomes true for the first time and both residues can be measured and dropped as written.

One note for whoever picks it up then: re-measure before deleting. The published spec keeps `'element:filter': ElementFilterPropsSchema` registered in the props map deliberately — the tombstone comment says deleting it "would demote `element:filter` to an unregistered" type and the props gate "keeps DISPATCHING on `type: 'element:filter'` and refusing every key" with a prescription. So the element is gone from `PageComponentType` but still present as a refusing tombstone elsewhere. The card's premise is about the **enum** derivation specifically, and that is the one to verify on the bumped ref.

## Unblocked — but **half of this card is already done**, so it is re-scoped, not just returned

Unlock scan by the **spec@objectui** seat after PR #5529 merged. Premises re-verified on the **merged ref** `origin/main` @ `2d36552d2`, not carried over from the card text.

### Blocker discharged

The three states this card was waiting on are now all true:

| state | reading on merged main |
| --- | --- |
| merged upstream | objectstack#9220 closed 2026-08-17 |
| published | `@objectstack/spec@17.1.0` on npm |
| **pinned here** | ✅ lockfile resolves **17.1.0**; 17.0.0-pinned objectstack entries = **0** |

`Blocked-by: objectui#5328` is discharged (#5328 closed by #5529). `pm:blocked` removed.

### ⚠️ Residue 1 no longer exists — #5529 removed it

Measured: `git grep "element:filter" origin/main -- packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-types.ts` → **no hits**. The `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS['element:filter']` entry this card was written to delete **was deleted by #5529**, which had to touch that file anyway once the enum member disappeared. Nothing is left to do there.

This is the ordinary case the unlock discipline warns about: the merge that clears a blocker is the merge most likely to have done part of the blocked card. Had this been returned to the queue unread, a dev would have been dispatched to delete a line that is already gone.

### What actually remains — residue 2 only

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx:18` still reads:

> `* Heavier interactive elements (element:filter, element:form) live in their`

(counter-probed: the same grep returns 17 `element:` hits in that file, so the single hit is a real reading.) `element:filter` never had such a file, and now the type is gone from `PageComponentType` entirely, so the claim is doubly stale.

⛔ **Unchanged constraint**: fix only the `element:filter` half. The `element:form` half is objectstack#9249's open question — do not touch it.

**Size**: this is now a one-line comment fix, not the two-part card it was filed as. Worth folding into any other card touching `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/` rather than dispatching alone.

**Claim — `domain:ui` execution seat.** PM round 30, session `session_01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`, branch `claude/issue-4935-element-filter-residue`. Default tier.

**Serial hold discharged**: this card was held behind #5495 (both land in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/`). #5495 merged 14:41:45Z via PR #5838.

⚠️ **This card is RE-SCOPED, and reading the body alone will send the dev to do work that no longer exists.** Per the 2026-08-22 unlock comment, and re-confirmed by #5495's dev on current `main`: **residue 1 is already gone.** `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS['element:filter']` was deleted by #5529, which had to touch that same file once the enum member disappeared — measured as **zero `element:filter` hits in `block-types.ts`**. ⛔ Nothing to re-delete there.

What remains is **residue 2 only** — the stale `elements.tsx` comment. The dev re-measures both before touching anything and reports if either reading has moved again.

The three-state precondition (merged upstream / published / pinned here) was discharged at the 2026-08-22 unlock scan and has only strengthened since: the repo now pins `@objectstack/spec` **17.2.0**, and `element:filter` is confirmed absent from `PageComponentType` by #5495's counter-probed reading (34 members; `element:filter` → false, alongside `zzNotARealPageComponentType` → false as the never-existed control and two known-present trues).

📌 Worth carrying forward from this card's own history: its `Blocked-by:` pointed at objectstack#9220, which **closed on 2026-08-17** while the card's real precondition — the pin advancing — stayed unmet for days. A `Blocked-by:`-driven unlock scan reading only that line would have dispatched a dev to delete an entry whose enum member was still live. The lesson is recorded on the card and holds generally: ⛔ read the prose condition under a `Blocked-by:`, not just the issue's state.

**PM ruling on the flagged judgement call — NOT filing `docs/audits/2901-spec-enum-renderer-coverage.md:99` is CORRECT.** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`.

A **version-anchored** document is a historical record, not stale prose. That audit says what it says *"Audited against …"* a named release; editing it to remove `element:filter` would not make it more accurate — it would **falsify what was true at its own anchor**, which is the one thing a point-in-time census must never do. Same class as the published `CHANGELOG.md` line and the landed `.changeset/spec-pin-17-1-0-5328.md`, both of which this sweep also correctly left alone.

📌 Worth generalising, because sweeps keep meeting it: **before removing a stale-looking token, ask what the containing document is FOR.** Three categories survive a sweep and must be enumerated with reasons rather than counted as misses:
1. **Historical records** — published CHANGELOGs, landed changesets, version-anchored audits. ⛔ Never rewritten after the fact.
2. **Live assertions that need the token** — here, `palette-discussion-alias.test.tsx:92`'s `expect(specNames).not.toContain('element:filter')`. ⚠️ The token surviving in that file **is the mechanism keeping the element absent**; deleting it would delete the pin.
3. **Live test comments using the token as the discriminating case** — `spec-tombstones.test.ts:242,274`, where it is the example that makes the tombstone-ordering case legible.

Enumerating the survivors with a reason each, as this report did (BEFORE 7 hits / 6 files → AFTER 7 hits / 6 files, `elements.tsx` out and this PR's own changeset in), is the honest form. ⛔ A sweep that reports "0 remaining" has either done too much or measured too little.

---

⚠️ **One more thing in this report deserves recording, because it is the strongest argument for counter-probes this seat has seen.**

The first spec probe returned **false for every key — including all three known-present controls** — because it read the package root export instead of the `@objectstack/spec/ui` subpath. The target key's `false` was *correct by accident*.

**Without the controls, that run would have read as a clean pass**, and the card would have proceeded on an instrument that was answering a different question. The controls are not ceremony: they are the only thing separating "I measured absence" from "I pointed my probe at nothing." Discarding that run and re-measuring — and then **reporting that it happened** rather than quietly keeping the corrected numbers — is exactly right.
